strengths: Elegant theoretical insight that Shapley values depend exclusively on the odd component of the value function decomposition, with clean and rigorous proof
First general theoretical justification for paired sampling heuristic, resolving an open conjecture from Fumagalli et al. (2026) that was limited to low-order interactions
Clever application of Fourier basis where odd/even properties align with cardinality parity, enabling clean decomposition and efficient implementation
Maintains consistency guarantee (convergence to true Shapley values as m → 2^d) while improving computational complexity from O(d^k·m) to O((d + m/η)²m)
State-of-the-art empirical performance with lowest average rank (1.50) across 8 benchmarks; particularly strong improvements on moderate-to-high-dimensional problems (up to 62× error reduction)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with thorough ablation studies and clear presentation of results with proper uncertainty quantification (median ± IQR)
Well-organized presentation with clear algorithm description and sound technical approach; all proofs appear correct
weaknesses: No finite-sample convergence rates or error bounds provided; only asymptotic consistency proven; unclear how approximation error scales with m, dimension d, and sparsity of true interactions

Critical dependence on GBT proxy model quality largely unanalyzed: no theoretical bounds on impact of proxy misspecification, false positive/negative rates in interaction selection, or robustness guarantees

Brief acknowledgment but insufficient exploration of even-odd correlation problem mentioned by Butler et al. (2025); discarding even components may lose information useful for odd approximation—impact not thoroughly investigated

Limited experimental scope: only d ≤ 101; no truly high-dimensional experiments (d >> 100); budgets m ≈ 100d not aggressive; low-budget regime (m < d·η) falls back to GBT and is underexplored; no comparison with higher-order PolySHAP (k ≥ 5)

Practical computational advantage unclear: while asymptotically better than PolySHAP, Figure 5 shows OddSHAP runtime comparable to RegressionMSR and substantially higher than LeverageSHAP; function evaluation (T_m) dominates regression cost, limiting practical benefit

Hyperparameter η lacks principled selection strategy: default η = 10 appears arbitrary; Figure 4 shows strong dataset dependence without clear guidance for practitioners to choose η without ground truth access
Missing finite-sample error analysis for approximation when true high-impact interactions are unknown; no bounds relating proxy quality to final Shapley value estimation error
No formal statistical significance testing; median ± IQR reported but unclear whether differences between methods are statistically significant when differences are small relative to IQR bands
